newsitem.title: USA: U.S. spot resid prices hold despite weak demand.
newsitem.headline: U.S. spot resid prices hold despite weak demand.

text.p: U.S. spot residual fuel prices held their relatively lofty levels again Thursday despite no major utility demand, still underpinned by a firm bunker market and higher NYMEX crude, industry sources said.

"There's still a premium for prompt oil, but there isn't any demand. There is some nervousness in the market," said one cash trader, noting firm bunkers, particulary on the East Coast, continued to support high sulphur grades.
In New York Harbor, physical one percent was still at $21.25 a barrel, with November paper sold early at $21.25 but quoted later at $21.50, up 25 cents with crude, traders said.
NYH December one percent paper also was talked about a quarter higher at about $21.70, traders said.
High sulphurs in New York remained firm with bunkers, with 2.2 percent still talked at about $20 though some thought the number could be even higher.
At the U.S. Gulf, prices held relatively steady, with one percent still at $20.00-25 and three percent at $20.25-50.
But one trader said USG high sulphurs may have peaked, citing talk any-October barrels may be offered below $20.
New York City gate gas prices were unchanged Thursday in the mid-$2.70s/mmBtu versus NYH one percent resid still at a $3.37/mmBtu equivalent.
